reviewer: Codex author source review; independent approval pending

owner_creation.analysis: OWN-10 separates borrowed process input from owned stdin backups, opened tty descriptors, popen streams, alternate-file names and allocated tag records. Shell handoff acquires a CLOEXEC backup before teardown.
owner_creation.invariant: Each FD, FILE pointer and saved string needs its own owner identity.
limitations: A standard numeric slot does not determine whether a descriptor was opened or borrowed.

aliases_escapes.analysis: OWN-10 save_curr_ifile increments a hold count and reedit releases that hold before trying saved/neighbor handles. Resource switching retains raw names and IFILE addresses across multiple owner operations.
aliases_escapes.invariant: Held handles require coherent list and disposal behavior.
limitations: The hold counter is not a Rust reference or generation check.

callback_targets.analysis: OWN-10 dispatches to system/popen and direct file/edit calls; no child owns the caller command allocation after the synchronous system return. Pipe streams have their own pclose lifecycle.
callback_targets.invariant: Native process calls must not inherit application owner pointers as live callbacks.
limitations: Child execution success is separate from parent resource cleanup success.

invalidation.analysis: OWN-10 close_file saves position, closes ch state and alternate pipes, clears alternate filename and then clears curr_ifile. Those operations invalidate different aliases at different points.
invalidation.invariant: A file switch must retire aliases before another owner uses them.
limitations: The sequence still relies on raw cross-module coordination.

mutation_commit.analysis: OWN-10 now checks backup acquisition and uses EINTR-aware dup2 for stdin swaps; restoration failure exits cooked rather than resuming the wrong input. M0-IO-003 and IND-FD-F3 stay open for maintained disposition.
mutation_commit.invariant: Do not dismantle stdin until its independent backup exists.
limitations: This records repaired source behavior without rerunning descriptor campaigns.

release_pair.analysis: OWN-10 releases shell command storage and backup FD after use, pairs pipe streams with pclose, and frees tag names/patterns before their nodes. These are distinct release operations, not one global destructor.
release_pair.invariant: Release counterparts must follow the resource acquired by each branch.
limitations: Process-exit reclamation is not evidence that every local release ran.

error_cleanup.analysis: OWN-10 pre-handoff backup failure returns before teardown; later stdin restoration failure emits a nonallocating diagnostic and _exit(1). General quit still performs broad mutable cleanup, including edit and history save.
error_cleanup.invariant: Error recovery must preserve the primary input resource or stop safely.
limitations: No complete cleanup ordering proof is claimed for fatal application allocation.

signals_handoff.analysis: OWN-10 terminate directly invokes quit, whereas process initialization restores inherited SIGPIPE and iread polls interrupt state through a guard. These mechanisms do not defer all owner cleanup to the main loop.
signals_handoff.invariant: Notification protocols cannot authorize asynchronous resource destruction.
limitations: The source route remains recorded under M0-SIG-003.

src/signal.rs.relationship: terminate at src/signal.rs:83-85 calls quit; OWN-10 includes the pager/edit/process resources that this asynchronous cleanup can reach.
